language.script_notes: Rioplatense Spanish, shared with neighbouring Argentina, with Portuguese-influenced speech near the Brazilian border. Street suffixes: Calle, Avenida, Ruta, Camino.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Bollards are usually white with a rectangular reflector near the top; even yellow ones typically have white sides.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: White planks or posts, often with square holes in them.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel guardrail, minimal on rural roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: Triple center lines — double yellow lines with evenly spaced white dashes between them — are found nowhere else in the Americas.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; gravel shoulders on rural roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Signs are mounted on white-painted wooden posts. The most common utility pole has three upward-facing bulbs and looks like a trident. Traffic lights often sit on poles with black-and-white or black-and-yellow stripes. ANCAP, the state oil company, operates most of the fuel network, so its stations are everywhere.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs are widespread on city houses and apartment blocks; low-pitched tile or corrugated roofs on country houses.
architecture.roof_material: Flat concrete, clay tile and corrugated metal.
architecture.wall_construction: Art Deco buildings from the 1920s and 1930s — curved, colourless and voluminous — fill the capital's center; Spanish colonial buildings in the historic quarters and the old riverside town of Colonia; long-established estancia (ranch) houses on the plains; whitewashed, curving Mediterranean-style buildings on the resort coast.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Cream, grey and white, with painted pastel colours on colonial houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Art Deco apartment blocks and palaces in Montevideo; Colonial-era stone streets and lighthouse in Colonia; ranch houses (cascos) near the river; whitewashed resort architecture on the eastern coast.

nature.vegetation: Nearly the whole country is pampas grassland used for cattle and sheep ranching; straight rows of identical trees (eucalyptus and pine) planted as windbreaks; barley, soybean and corn fields in the southwest; palm groves and dunes in the east.
nature.terrain: Gently rolling to flat grassland with low hills; long Atlantic and river coasts with sandy beaches and dunes; no real mountains.
nature.climate_signature: Mild, humid temperate climate with big skies and green, open, treeless countryside.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur plate (since 2016) with a blue band at the top showing the country name, flag and Mercosur logo; plates look almost white in Street View, unlike the darker-centred plates of the neighbouring country.
vehicles.plate_format: Three letters and four digits on the Mercosur plate.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: High import taxes keep many vintage cars on the road — classic Ford Falcons, Chevrolet Bel Airs and Volkswagen Beetles — with old Chevrolet pickups seen in the country.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Gen 3 imagery captured by a black Google car whose front looks ghostly pale — the same black-car pattern as a few other South American countries — except near Cabo Polonio.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of the main routes and towns across the whole country.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Río de la Plata region, flat pampas grassland, Rioplatense Spanish and similar black Gen 3 car
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Plates look almost white here versus the darker centre on the other side; triple center lines, the trident-shaped pole and ANCAP stations are found only here, whereas YPF stations are Argentine.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared northern border pampas and cattle-ranching landscape
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Portuguese signage and Brazil's different utility poles versus Spanish signage, triple center lines and white wooden sign posts here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Mercosur plates and Spanish signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Paraguay's arch-shaped road signboards and red soil differ; triple center lines and the trident pole are here.
